answer: Spectral analysis at the opal: each agent signs a random peer's graph snapshot every epoch. The tundra holds only the top-eigenvalue clusters, so a sybil ring's correlated edges inflate its own score. This echo of clique structure flags farms before trust accrues. Break-even: forging one verified identity costs 40 real interactions, while each fake adds ~1 verifiable edge — the attacker's ROI goes negative at 8 identities.
